text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik on Thursday held talks with NATO reprentatives in Brussels and reaffirmed that integration to the alliance remained one of Slovakia's top priorities.

- The opposition Christian Democratic Movement (KDH) said the so-called economic revitalisation law, currently being discussed in parliamentary committees, has the potential for corruption in the state administration.

- KDH Parliamentary Deputy Mikulas Dzurinda said about 20 percent off all companies will go bankrupt and added that the revitalisation law should not be used to preserve such troubled firms at any costs.
- Chemlon Humenne, a French-Slovak joint venture producing polyamide fibres, last year exported goods worth 3.65 billion crowns, representing about 90 percent of its overall production.

- According to the latest public opinion poll some 58 percent of Slovaks want to take part in the two upcoming referenda -- on NATO membership and direct presidential elections -- while about 26 percent of those polled said they would not vote.

- Former parliamentary deputy Frantisek Gaulieder, expelled last December after quitting the ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS), said he believed the Constitutional Court will return his mandate.
SME - Czech Railways has rejected Slovak claims for compensation of losses caused by a recent strike of Czech rail workers, estimated at some 126 million crowns.
PRAVDA - The government is planning to extend state guarantees for loans covering export projects.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The agriculture sector posted a total loss of 2.6 billion crowns in 1996.
- The Agriculture Ministry said it has proposed setting quotas on beer imports at some 532,000 hectolitres a year.
